## SHIELD reference-workflow checkpoint (2026-09-17)

A failed SHIELD stage-3 calibration was initially presented as a shared-storage
interruption because the launcher caught any `run.calibration()` error, replaced
its message with a write-interruption explanation, and retried. Direct checks of
the output roots and lower-level file operations did not reproduce a storage
failure. The same calibration then failed against a local output root, and the
failure was traced to a likelihood term with a zero denominator. This incident
joins three reproducibility questions that were previously being treated
separately: whether the real error remains observable, whether the scientific
inputs and environment can be reconstructed, and whether an interrupted
calibration follows the same stochastic path when resumed.

Current `jheem_analyses` `master` changes the future-growth ratio denominator from
`start` to `start + 1` in
[`55bd55c6`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/55bd55c6975c09063c8c62828bf52f6a9da31eb3).
That makes the immediate division finite but also defines scientific behavior for
zero and small baselines. Engineering work may reproduce the edge cases, preserve
the original error, and add characterization or non-finite-likelihood checks. A
different formula, pseudocount, exclusion rule, or expected value should not be
selected through an infrastructure change; the intended behavior needs explicit
scientific review before it becomes a regression assertion.

The sampler currently lacks a coherent explicit-seed contract. At
[`bayesian.simulations@4e0d13e`](https://github.com/tfojo1/bayesian.simulations/commit/4e0d13e85857396bb0e6e2ac1d244775b2145f75):

- `create.mcmc.cache(seed = ...)` validates `seed` but does not pass it to
  `do.create.cache()`, whose signature requires it;
- `do.create.chain.cache.controls(..., seed)` accepts the value but generates
  per-chunk seeds with `runif()` from ambient R state rather than from that
  argument; and
- `jheem2::set.up.calibration()` exposes no seed argument, so current application
  setup relies on prior global RNG state.

Per-chunk seed storage was introduced in
[`b170ce7`](https://github.com/tfojo1/bayesian.simulations/commit/b170ce7e5c265fa7540a2847a8bc894fa797dd2c),
after the `34840866` revision currently installed by the container base lock.
Consequently, the existing container canary proves that a partial cache can be
continued to its remaining chunk; it does not prove that an explicit seed controls
the schedule, that interrupted and uninterrupted traces are equal, or that the
same request is reproducible across the team's servers.

Two review branches establish useful but incomplete evidence:

- [`jheem_analyses@accd7b64`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/accd7b64dd0ab1f38f5ccad993a643c3c7544de2)
  stages automatic provenance, immutable source declarations, read-only manager
  caches, truthful failure/resume behavior, and a bounded SHIELD canary. It split
  from `master` at `ea111ea3` and must be reconciled with later application work,
  including the likelihood change, before it can be proposed for ordinary use.
- [`jheem-containers@262c733`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/commit/262c733d5c71ec4aa480dde4131880002105dc31)
  builds a pinned SHIELD image and has completed a real-engine preflight plus a
  forced-interruption/resume canary in CI. The image still pins the older sampler,
  the canary is a tiny stage-0 path rather than the failing stage-3 path, and no
  uninterrupted-versus-resumed or cross-server equality comparison is made.

These are validation assets, not yet evidence that SHIELD calibration is
reproducible. The 2026-09-17 sequence prioritized a small, executable sampler
seed demonstration and focused correction before SHIELD branch reconciliation.
The narrower container-pilot sequence is updated below; it does not remove the
sampler prerequisite for a deterministic-replay claim.

## SHIELD container-pilot update (2026-09-22)

The team is evaluating containerization of SHIELD as an operational deliverable.
That question is narrower than whether an earlier calibration can be reproduced
exactly. The [existing container spike](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/blob/262c733d5c71ec4aa480dde4131880002105dc31/workloads/shield/README.md)
builds a pinned image and exercises a small real-engine calibration through a
forced interruption and checkpoint continuation in hosted CI. It has not yet
run on a team server, completed production-sized simset assembly there, or
compared uninterrupted and resumed scientific traces.

The spike pins `jheem_analyses@accd7b64`, while the verified active branch is
`master@16eff985`, 71 commits ahead of the common base with the staged
`codex/shield-source-readiness` branch. The active SHIELD tree now has a
[three-tier model-test workflow](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/.github/workflows/test-shield.yml)
and a [calibration launcher](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/shield_calib_setup_and_run.R)
that prints the original error and stops on many non-storage failures. Those
changes supersede parts of the staged branch, but ordinary setup still defaults
to clearing state and uses a fixed `set.seed(0)` before calibration. The
[source bootstrap](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/shield_source_code.R)
still requires a sibling `jheem2` checkout on `dev` in source mode, and can pull
when interactive. A recorded container run needs an explicit, non-mutating
source and run-mode contract; the older branch supplies candidate pieces, not a
merge-ready replacement for the current application.

The new test workflow is useful characterization, not yet a dependable green
gate: the [2026-09-22 run](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/actions/runs/35762822719)
failed in the static tier and skipped the later tiers. Its
[README](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/tests/README.md)
says some tests intentionally fail to preserve open code-review findings. At
least one static test asserts that the `+1` growth-penalty denominator should be
removed and suggests alternatives; because that is a scientific formula choice,
it should be resolved by the scientific owners, not silently changed as
container-readiness work.

A clean local checkout of the same pinned analyses commit reproduced 11 static
assertion failures and 3 static skips. Running the unit-file subset independently
returned 6 assertion failures, 4 errors, and 4 skips; missing test-bootstrap
inputs account for some of those errors and skips, so these counts are not a
model-defect count. The workflow chains static → unit → integration with `needs`,
which means a persistently red static tier prevents the model tier from running.
Conversely, the
[test runner](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/tests/run_tests.R#L94-L114)
exits nonzero only for failed assertions or errors: if required bootstrap stages
are unavailable and tests only skip, a tier can appear green without exercising
its intended model path. Before using this workflow as a container acceptance
gate, separate open diagnostic findings from must-pass checks and make missing
required integration prerequisites fail explicitly. Text matching for a local
`set.seed()` call and the growth-penalty formula test are examples that need a
contract-level or domain-reviewed assertion rather than an automatic code edit.

A bounded pilot should therefore establish, in order: a pinned image built
against current SHIELD source; identified manager assets and source revisions;
non-destructive fresh/resume behavior; successful real-engine preflight and a
small checkpoint continuation; then a retained run on a team server that checks
mounts, file ownership, error logs, runtime, and output inspection. Full assembly
and repeated-run comparisons are separate acceptance steps. The sampler seed
finding remains recorded and should be tested before claiming deterministic
replay or equivalent results across servers.

## Recorded-run source checkpoint (2026-09-23)

[`jheem_analyses@5b377e8`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/5b377e8)
is on the isolated
[`codex/shield-recorded-contract` branch](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/tree/codex/shield-recorded-contract),
not `master`. It adds an opt-in `SHIELD_RECORDED_RUN=true` route through the
current source bootstrap and calibration launcher. That route requires declared
source commit identities, immutable dated manager releases, verified offline
manager assets, separate input and output roots, and an explicit seed. Fresh
mode refuses existing calibration state; resume requires a matching input
receipt and readable checkpoint/progress before MCMC. A focused cache change
allows verified offline assets to load from a read-only cache without a writer
lock. The default ordinary route remains selected without the opt-in flag.
The branch changes no likelihood formula or model parameter. Its
[pilot contract and caveats](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/5b377e8/applications/SHIELD/RECORDED-RUN-PILOT.md)
remain review material, not supported production instructions.

This branch addresses the **prepared-runtime and input-identity** portion of
the broader [run-record contract](reproducibility.qmd#proposed-target-contract).
Its local `inputs.json` is not the staged automatic attempt history, an
output-linked simset receipt, or a durable archive. The container pilot should
prove that this narrow route can execute and continue safely; it must not make
the separate provenance and sampler work appear complete. A supported team
workflow should eventually supply the technical declarations behind the
existing calibration command rather than require operators to manage another
set of identifiers by hand.

Focused runtime and cache tests passed locally; the existing SHIELD static
suite still had 12 diagnostic failures and lacked local bootstrap data for its
full path. The current modular launcher is deliberately rejected in recorded
mode because it clears calibration state. The older container canary calls
that modular launcher and expects an older runtime interface and stage-0
fixture, so merely changing its analyses commit would neither run nor validate
this branch. The next gate is to reconcile the container preflight and canary
with the current recorded entrypoint, run a must-pass hosted smoke, and only
then attempt a retained team-server pilot. No deterministic-replay or
production-calibration claim follows from the source branch alone.

## Container canary and shield2 pilot (2026-09-29)

The recorded-run branch was rebased onto current `master`. Two source changes
followed. The recorded state check had rebuilt the calibration directory as
`mcmc_runs/<version>/<location>/<code>`, but `jheem2@ccb1f9b` reorders it to
`<version>/<code>/<location>`, so `resume` would have looked in the wrong
place; the check now asks jheem2 for the directory once jheem2 is loaded.
And a two-iteration `container.smoke.stage0` calibration (the real SHIELD model
and stage-0 likelihood, two parameters) is registered only when a recorded run
sets `SHIELD_ENABLE_CONTAINER_SMOKE=true`.

The container build in `jheem-containers` PR #24 was pointed at that source.
Its hosted CI now builds the recorded image, runs preflight (declared source
revisions, immutable manager releases, verified manager digests), starts a
fresh calibration, kills it once the first checkpoint is durable, and resumes
it in a separate process until the second checkpoint is durable, checking
that the first was not rewritten. It deliberately stops there. A 2-iteration
run peaks above the 16 GB hosted runner's memory while building the MCMC
summary (the kernel killed R at 15.5 GB resident), so summary and assembly are
server tests. Two test defects surfaced and were fixed: a digest comparison
that failed on an attribute, and a checkpoint check that required the control
file to be strictly newer than the chunk. Kernel timestamps are coarse, so the
control saved right after a chunk can share its timestamp.

The image CI tested (exported as an artifact, image ID `214b9677…`) was loaded
into rootless Podman on shield2 under an administrator's account:

| Run | Local-disk state | NAS state |
|---|---|---|
| Canary calibration, uninterrupted through summary and assembly | passed, 342 s | passed, 368 s |
| Kill after the first checkpoint, resume to the second | passed | passed |
| Memory: loading / sampling / summary and assembly | about 5.9 / 10.3 / 28 GB | about 5.9 / 10.3 / 28.5 GB |

Chunk files are about 265 MB each and take about 54 s to write; the global
control is about 154 MB. Writing a chunk takes longer than a sampling iteration
at this size. The simulation set is 270 MB. The stage-0 run below shows these
sizes, and the summary and assembly memory, were inflated by the image's
package installation, since fixed.

Server prerequisites observed on the RHEL 9 hosts, recorded in the server
administration repository:

- Podman is installed and Docker is not. Rootless runs use `--userns=keep-id`
  so outputs keep the user as owner; local bind mounts need an SELinux relabel.
- A rootless container is stopped about 10 seconds after its user's last login
  session ends unless lingering is enabled for that user
  (`loginctl enable-linger`). A pilot container was lost this way before
  lingering was enabled.
- Containers reach the CIFS-mounted NAS only with the `virt_use_samba` SELinux
  boolean enabled on the host, and write to it only when the container keeps
  the user's `jheem` group (`--group-add keep-groups`); without it, writes are
  refused. Both prerequisites were enabled for this pilot on shield2 only.

## Realistic stage on shield2 (2026-09-30)

`calib.9.28.stage0` for C.12580 (15,000 iterations, 30 chunks) ran in the same
image on shield2 with NAS state, one BLAS thread, and the ordinary launcher's
checkpoint settings, alongside the team's completed native run of the same
stage and location on shield1:

| | Container, shield2 | Native, shield1 |
|---|---|---|
| Result | exit 0; summary and 300-simulation set written | complete |
| Time per 500-iteration chunk | median 27.6 min (25.9–29.4) | median 29.9 min (28.8–30.9), 10 locations sharing the server |
| Sampling | 13 h 46 min at about 10.5 GB | about 15 h |
| Summary and assembly | about 12 min, peak 35.4 GB | not measured |
| Chunk file | about 305 MB | about 44 MB |
| Simulation set | 1.54 GB | 1.28 GB |

Runtime and stability are comparable. The image's analyses revision is
slightly newer than the one the native run started from, so likelihood values
are not compared.

The chunk difference was not in the number of simulations. In the container's
first chunk, the first stored simulation serialized to about 5.6 GB against
about 20 MB natively. The cause was the image installing the team packages
with kept source references. Each jheem2 R6 object stored in a simulation
(specification, solver, and run metadata) has methods whose source reference
points at the package source file, and that file's text was an unforced lazy-load
promise; saving it serialized about 2.8 GB of the package's lazy-load state per
object. Native runs source jheem2 under `Rscript`, which keeps no source
references. R's default package install doesn't keep them either.

The image now installs `distributions`, `bayesian.simulations`, `locations`, and
jheem2 with `R CMD INSTALL --without-keep.source`, fails its build if any of
them keeps source references, and pins `bayesian.simulations` and
`distributions` to the commits the team servers run (the base image had carried
an older `bayesian.simulations` without its July and August 2025 fixes). The
hosted canary now fails if its first chunk exceeds 100 MB. The same canary on
shield2 with NAS state (`jheem-containers@93bf24e`):

| | Before the fix | After the fix |
|---|---|---|
| Elapsed | 368 s | 101 s |
| Peak memory (summary and assembly) | 28.5 GB | 11.1 GB |
| Checkpoint chunk | 266 MB | 5.4 MB |
| Simulation set (2 simulations) | 270 MB | 9.6 MB |

The earlier 28 GB and 35 GB peaks therefore described the image, not SHIELD. A
full stage has not been rerun with the fixed image.

## Integration checkpoint and next sequence (2026-10-01)

The September 30 implementation adds input/output lineage, per-attempt records,
and sequential single-chain stages
([analyses `373faf27`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/373faf2775f584093ac16c17ce18432959c609d9),
[containers `ad92324`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/commit/ad92324f7d742d2059a31aac65a9b51e1d23c528)).
The [hosted canary](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/36776425076)
now completes summary and assembly, checks the records, and runs a two-stage
pipeline. The operator wrapper and runbook are in the container repository.
This newer path has not yet been exercised by another operator on a team server.

A negative check found a boundary defect: deleting the summary
and simulation-set files while retaining `outputs.json` still lets the pipeline
report all stages complete. The preceding-stage resolver hashes the record but
does not verify the files it describes. Completion and lineage checks therefore
needed to verify record identity and referenced output sizes and digests before
reusing a stage. A successful ordinary canary did not cover that failure mode.

That defect is now fixed in
[`jheem_analyses@06505412`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/06505412ff4ad870ba0263361b791ba5d53737de),
integrated into `master` through
[`3f463e2a`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/3f463e2ab274e4d5e24decdf82f294a91b628857).
The matching container implementation was integrated into `main` through
[`4b9f83db`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/commit/4b9f83dbab3f784aa177947e2c27925d784eae10).
The source branch includes current application changes and verified latest-loader
integration; this increment changes no likelihood formula or sampler behavior.

[Run 36815091235](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/actions/runs/36815091235)
passed the offline runtime/cache tests, real-engine interruption/resume,
summary and assembly, and a two-stage pipeline. Missing simsets, same-size
modified simsets, and a changed requested seed were each rejected. Restoring
the original files and inputs allowed verified reuse. Focused tests also cover
stale preceding-stage records and interrupted setup without a checkpoint.
The ordinary SHIELD static suite still fails on existing findings and skips
later tiers; these operational checks do not resolve its scientific assertions.

The exact tested image is retained in the non-latest
[`shield-pilot-2026.10.01-r36815091235` prerelease](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/releases/tag/shield-pilot-2026.10.01-r36815091235),
beyond the seven-day Actions artifact lifetime. The release contains the image
archive and `IMAGE.txt` with its identity and source revisions. Its published
archive SHA-256 matches the tested export:
`01e344d5948945851f397a41e2ec24b5f77878e2335b5d8960eb5a5a3a81e60c`.
This retains the runtime, not scientific outputs or their run records; canary
logs and records remain in their temporary CI artifact.

Next:

1. Have another team member launch, interrupt, resume, and locate outputs from
   the runbook. Run one representative full stage with the corrected image to
   measure its production-size memory and output sizes. The earlier cross-server
   timings establish feasibility, not a controlled speed or equivalence result.
2. Complete the stage-3 boundary: either support and verify multiple chains or
   document and test the handoff from isolated container outputs to the native
   workflow. Recorded mode currently refuses multi-chain calibrations. Shared
   writers also require a cross-process locking strategy, beyond the wrapper's
   same-account container check.

A stronger same-seed replay claim follows a separate sampler increment:
demonstrate the present seed-forwarding behavior, correct it with focused
same-seed/different-seed and uninterrupted/resumed tests in
`bayesian.simulations`, then compare traces under one image digest and across
the servers. The operational pilot need not wait for that claim, but must not
imply it.

## Open questions and destination

- Which realistic stage and location should follow the canary, and what
  runtime and memory difference from the ordinary launcher is acceptable?
- Which current model checks can become a reliable must-pass operational
  subset, and which assertions require scientific review?
- After same-image equality is tested, which scientific outputs and tolerances
  define equivalence across materially different numerical platforms?
- What scientific behavior is intended for the future-growth penalty when its
  baseline is zero or near zero?

The runtime adapter, container build, tests, and server runbook belong in
`jheem_analyses` and `jheem-containers`. This page remains the cross-repository
investigation until a retained server pilot uses a current pinned image and the
owning repositories document its supported path; then it can be reduced to
the durable contract and result.
